b.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's morning weather log, running on Tolu's laptop.

  1. Start n8n. With Africa/Lagos chosen and the volume ticked in Card 3, the commands are: 
    docker volume create n8n_data

docker run -it --name n8n -p 5678:5678 \
  -e GENERIC_TIMEZONE="Africa/Lagos" -e TZ="Africa/Lagos" \
  -e N8N_ENFORCE_SETTINGS_FILE_PERMISSIONS=true -e N8N_RUNNERS_ENABLED=true \
  -v n8n_data:/home/node/.n8n \
  n8nio/n8n
  2. Build HL · Morning weather → Sheet: Schedule Trigger (Days, every 1, 6am, minute 30) → HTTP Request (GET, the Open-Meteo URL for 7.38, 3.94) → Edit Fields (date, max_temp_c, rain_chance, rain_mm, advice, all in Expression mode with [0]) → Google Sheets · Append Row, Map Automatically, into HL Weather.
  3. Test, then publish. Execute workflow, check the row, then Save and Publish.
  4. Restart test. Stop the container, start it again (docker start -a n8n), log in: the workflow and the Google credential are still listed.

Evidence: a screenshot of Executions showing a run at 06:30 that you didn't start, and the HL Weather row for that date, for example 2026-10-05 | 30.4 | 78 | 5.3 | Rain likely: pack tarpaulins, start deliveries early. Log your volume name (n8n_data) and "data survived restart: yes".
mistakes: Running the container without -v n8n_data:/home/node/.n8n, so the restart test wipes the owner account and workflow.
Leaving the timezone unset, so the 06:30 run lands at about 11:30 or 12:30 Lagos time.
Clicking Save and Execute workflow but never Publish, so Executions only ever shows manual runs.
Letting the laptop sleep or closing Docker Desktop overnight, then concluding the schedule is broken.
b.pass: Executions shows a run at about 06:30 that the learner didn't start, the HL Weather sheet has that date's row with numbers (not [30.4] or {{ }} text), and the log says the workflow and credential survived a container restart.
b.redo: Send it back if the only runs are manual tests, the run time is off by hours, or there is no proof of the restart test.

s.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's "Become a supply partner" form, rebuilt in n8n as HL · Partner form → Leads.

  1. Form Trigger. Title "Become a Harvest Lane supply partner". Four required fields: Name (text), Phone (text), Business type (dropdown: hotel, restaurant, caterer, school, other), Message (textarea). The trigger names each output field after its label, so check the Output panel for the exact keys.
  2. Edit Fields · Clean lead (all values in Expression mode): 
    name           {{ $json.Name.trim() }}
phone          {{ '+234' + $json.Phone.replace(/\D/g, '').replace(/^234/, '').replace(/^0/, '') }}
business_type  {{ $json["Business type"] }}
message        {{ $json.Message }}
received_at    {{ $now.toFormat('yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm') }}
    The phone line strips every non-digit, then any leading 234 or 0, then adds +234 once.
  3. Google Sheets · Append Row on a copy of the Leads sheet (never the live one), headers matching the five field names, Map Automatically.
Phone typedStored
08031234567+2348031234567
0803 123 4567+2348031234567
+234 803-123-4567+2348031234567
2348031234567+2348031234567
(0803) 123.4567+2348031234567

Use made-up names and numbers for all five test leads.

Cost note for the log: n8n counts 5 executions for 5 leads, however many nodes (and unlimited when self-hosted). A Zapier version with a Formatter step and a Sheets step uses 2 tasks per lead, so 10 tasks. Count the action steps in your own Boss 1 Zap and multiply by 5.
mistakes: Using a messy-phone rule that only handles a leading 0, so +234 or 234 numbers come out as +234234… .
Writing the expression with the field in Fixed mode, so the sheet stores the literal {{ }} text.
Testing on the live Leads sheet or with real customers' numbers instead of a copy and made-up data.
Giving the Zapier comparison as a guess, without counting the action steps in the Zap.
s.pass: Five rows in the Leads copy, every phone in +234XXXXXXXXXX form (including the messy one), a received_at on each, and a written line comparing n8n executions with Zapier tasks based on a stated step count.
s.redo: Send it back if any phone is double-prefixed or unchanged, if a field holds expression text, or if real personal data was used.

g.answer:
Worked example: a learner imports a seven-node "daily RSS digest to email" template (free services only) and adapts it for Harvest Lane's morning food-price news.

Node-by-node notes (the part a beginner must be able to follow):

NodeInDoesOut
Schedule TriggerNothingStarts the run every day at 07:001 item with the time
RSS ReadThe trigger itemFetches the news feedAbout 20 items, one per article
Filter20 articlesKeeps articles from the last 24 hoursAbout 6 items
Edit Fields6 articlesKeeps title, link, date6 tidy items
Limit6 itemsKeeps the first 55 items
Aggregate5 itemsJoins them into one list1 item
Send Email1 itemEmails the list to Tolu1 sent email

The change: the template had no timezone and a hard-coded recipient. Fix: set the workflow timezone to Africa/Lagos in workflow settings, and move the recipient into an Edit Fields "Settings" node at the start so it is changed in one place.

Test evidence: before the fix, the schedule used n8n's default timezone (America/New_York), so a 07:00 trigger would fire at about 12:00 in Lagos; after it, Executions shows the run at 07:00 and one email arrives in Tolu's test inbox.

Submit: the exported workflow JSON (no keys pasted in fields), your notes table, and before/after screenshots of the changed setting and the test execution.
mistakes: Choosing a template that needs a paid API key, then skipping the nodes that fail.
Writing notes that repeat the node name ("the Filter node filters") instead of what goes in and comes out.
Making the change but not running it again, so there is no before/after evidence.
Sharing an export with a key typed into a node field instead of stored in a credential.
g.pass: A template of six or more nodes runs on test data, every node has an in/does/out sentence a beginner could follow, and one Harvest Lane change is shown with a passing test execution.
g.redo: Send it back if notes skip nodes, the change is untested, or the export contains a pasted key.
